beats.text: Every time you run a long-context LLM, your VRAM is being shredded by fragmented KV cache, wasting up to 80% of your precious GPU memory.
beats.visual_focus: A memory bar chart showing massive gaps of empty space between allocated blocks.

visual_blueprint.title: MEMORY FRAGMENTATION
visual_blueprint.sub: Standard allocation leads to massive overhead

motif_params.title: MEMORY FRAGMENTATION
motif_params.sub: Standard allocation leads to massive overhead

beats.text: Why? Because static memory allocation is like a hotel that refuses to rent out half-empty rooms, forcing guests to wait in the lobby forever.
beats.visual_focus: A hotel floor plan where rooms are locked and guests are stuck in a queue.

beats.text: Enter Paged Attention: it treats your KV cache like OS virtual memory, mapping non-contiguous blocks to physical VRAM using a clever page table system.
beats.visual_focus: A pointer diagram showing a logical sequence mapping to scattered physical memory blocks.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook is solid—mentioning VRAM shredding immediately caught my attention because I've definitely hit OOM errors while playing with local LLMs. I liked the hotel analogy in Beat 2; it wasn't patronizing, it actually explained the fragmentation issue well. Beat 4 was the only part where I had to pause, but since you mentioned 'page tables' and 'kernel logic,' it felt like actual dev talk rather than marketing fluff. It's a good breakdown.
